videos.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate 2020 (freeCodeCamp full course) — AWS Global Infrastructure section
transcript_key_points: Region = geographic area with multiple isolated AZs
AZ = discrete data centers with redundant power/networking
Edge locations cache content via CloudFront; not for running compute
Region choice: latency, compliance/data residency, service availability, cost

videos.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate 2020 (freeCodeCamp full course) — Shared Responsibility Model section
transcript_key_points: AWS: security OF the cloud (hardware, facilities, virtualization)
Customer: security IN the cloud (data, OS, IAM, firewall config)
Responsibility shifts with service model: IaaS vs PaaS vs SaaS

transcript_key_points: Public vs private vs hybrid deployment
IaaS (EC2) vs PaaS (Elastic Beanstalk) vs SaaS (WorkMail) — who manages what

videos.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate 2020 (freeCodeCamp full course) — IAM deep-dive: users, groups, roles, policies
videos.credit: freeCodeCamp.org — 'AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate 2020' by Andrew Brown (ExamPro). Used with attribution; not re-uploaded.
videos.lesson_topic: IAM fundamentals: users vs groups vs roles, identity-based vs resource-based policies, policy structure
transcript_key_points: Users = long-term identities; groups bundle users; roles = temporary credentials via STS
Policies are JSON: Effect, Action, Resource; managed vs inline
Attach policies to groups/roles, not individual users

videos.lesson_topic: MFA, root user lockdown, least-privilege principle, credential hygiene
transcript_key_points: Enable MFA on root first; never use root daily; no root access keys
Least privilege: minimum permissions for the job; rotate credentials
Password policy; credential report and Access Advisor

transcript_key_points: EC2 instance profiles: roles inject temporary credentials into instances
Cross-account access via assumable roles; trust policy = who can assume
Evaluation: explicit deny > allow > implicit deny
